'''Memory diskettes''' were [[Droid/Legends|droid]] parts that functioned as the central processing area of a unit.<ref name="TO">{{StoryCite|story=Troublesome Outing|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 5}}</ref> Such pieces of technology were similar to the [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]] and the [[Verbobrain/Legends|verbobrains]].<ref name="EGD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> [[Professor/Legends|Professor]] [[Cantebarius H. Broom]], a deranged [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], was known to deactivate droids by removing their memory diskettes.<ref name="TO" />

==Behind the scenes==
The memory diskettes were first mentioned in ''[[Troublesome Outing]]'',<ref name="TO" /> a [[Wikipedia:Spain|Spanish]] story of undetermined [[canon]]icity that was published in [[1986]].<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/droids-and-ewoks-return-spains-lost-star-wars-comic-strips|text=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost ''Star Wars'' Comic Strips|int=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost Star Wars Comic Strips|nolive=1}}</ref> [[Abel G. Peña]], who translated the story in [[Wikipedia:English language|English]] for the first time in [[2013]], referred to the use of the word "diskette" as a "quaint anachronism." In the 1980s, massive-memory cloud storage and flash drives were still inconceivable. But nowadays, diskettes look out of place in the futuristic ''Star Wars'' universe.<ref name="Hasslein">{{Blogspot|subdomain=hassleinbooks|url=2013/03/guest-blog-ee-chee-wa-maa-translating.html|name=Hasslein Blog|text=Ee Chee Wa Maa! Translating Spain's Long-Lost Ewoks and Droids Comics}}</ref>
